requirements.title: Subnet configuration enforces bounds at create and update boundaries
Governance configuration is owner-only and enforces contract + timelock bounds
Owner-action queue enforces authorization, expiry, cancellation, and queued-by binding
Pause mode blocks stake-changing actions but preserves reveal/challenge liveness
Stake accounting and validator eligibility remain conservative under adversarial input
Commit/reveal is domain-bound and rejects mismatched epochs/salts/mechanisms
Pending commitments lock withdrawal/unregister until reveal or challenge resolution
Expired-commit slashing is bounded and self-challenge cannot extract bounty
Subnet epoch emission schedule can only be paid for finalized epochs once
Mechanism emission lanes enforce mechanism-id bounds and finalized-epoch payout
Batch policy queue lifecycle enforces governance auth, delay, cancel, expiry, and queue-origin binding
Fee policy queue and bounds enforce capped protocol fee and queue-origin safety
Batch commit requires enabled policy, eligible proposer, and current epoch
Fee funding cannot exceed declared total and pre-finalize withdrawal is bounded
Batch finalization credits proposer bond refund and distributes fees from snapshotted policy
Leaf settlement enforces index bounds, valid merkle proof, and one-time settlement
Replay/duplicate challenges slash proposer bond and enforce prior-finalized checks
Inference leaf helper is domain-separated by subnet/mechanism/epoch/request/result
Domain subnet validation rejects invalid topology and fee/delay bounds
Domain stake transitions are conservative and reject overdraw
Domain commitment verification enforces reveal timing and binding
Domain epoch/slash math remains bounded across edge values
Verifier admission actions enforce delay, cancellation, expiry, and governance-generation binding
Delayed deprecation stops new tasks at execution while preserving existing-task settlement
Fee policy caps success fees and couples zero-fee mode to a zero treasury
Task admission and request nullifiers reject invalid bounds and requester-local replay
Proof settlement binds the canonical journal, program, result, selector, and proof envelope
Permissionless proof relay pays only the proved beneficiary and verifier failure is state-atomic
An open task closes exactly once through settlement or a fee-free terminal refund
Adapter and base-verifier availability are code-hash pinned and fail closed into full refund
Pull claims enforce bounds, rollback failed transfers, and prevent reentrant withdrawal
Funded value, escrow, settlements, refunds, claims, fees, and open-task counters remain exact
RISC Zero V3 identity, version, selector, and direct-verifier runtime hash are pinned at admission
Verification binds the program, SHA-256 journal, selector, exact V3 seal envelope, and base code
Base-verifier runtime drift is reported to settlement for fail-closed task liveness
